subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Carter <john.carter@finly.com>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@finly.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency

Hi John & Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Per our discussion, wanted to capture the key pain points, success criteria, and immediate next steps so we’re aligned. Notes below — I’ve attached a short PDF with raw call notes.

Key pain points
- Streaming UX feels “chunky” at peak times: customers see multi-second gaps between tokens and an almost-immediate buffering experience on mobile.
- p95 tail latency is highly variable (observed 350–800ms on initial token during spikes).
- Concurrency spikes during batch transactions (billing runs) cause throughput collapse and request queuing.
- Current stack: Finly routes generation through OpenAI + in-house microservices that add 60–120ms of overhead; no prefix caching today.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- End-to-end p95 for streaming token delivery < 250ms under normal peak load.
- First-byte streaming latency < 150ms for 95th percentile.
- Support 300 concurrent streaming sessions with < 10% degradation in latency.
- Maintain model-quality delta within ~3% vs current outputs (accuracy/response quality).

Constraints & data points you shared
- Avg request length ~600 tokens, peak bursts every hour (5–10m) where concurrent streams jump from ~60 to ~250.
- Token budget sensitivity: cost per 1M tokens is a key procurement metric.

Immediate next steps
1) Redwood: deliver short architecture recommendation (hosted vs dedicated) + rough capacity estimate and PoC plan by Tue (attached).
2) Finly: share traffic sample CSV and any test user accounts for load testing (you mentioned Sara could share).
3) Align on PoC goals & SLOs; proposed target: 2-week PoC with clear perf tests (p95 latency, streaming first-byte, concurrency soak).

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf

If I missed anything, please call out edits. I’ll loop in Aditya (serving/runtime) and Michael (pricing/dedicated capacity) so they can scope the technical and commercial sides.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: John Carter <john.carter@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@finly.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications / asks from our side: 

- Current traffic: ~1k DAU, but peak concurrency historically ~200–260 for 10–15 minute windows; we expect this to grow ~30% over the next 6 months.
- Average output length is ~600 tokens; some workflows go to 2k tokens but are rarer.
- Streaming is critical for our chat UX; users abandon sessions after ~3s of perceived stall.
- We’d prefer a PoC window of 2 weeks with validated test scripts and our synthetic traffic.

Questions:
1) Do you expect Redwood Hosted to meet these SLOs, or will Dedicated capacity be required to hit 250ms p95 reliably?
2) What telemetry will you need from us (sample traffic, auth tokens, test accounts) to run an honest load test?

I’ve uploaded a small traffic sample (finly-traffic-sample.csv) that shows our per-minute concurrency from last week — hope that helps.

Best,
John
John Carter
Head of Product, Finly
john.carter@finly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency

Aditya / Michael — forwarding Finly notes and the sample CSV John attached. High level asks below; can you both take a pass and send bullet responses by EOD Monday? I’ll consolidate and send back to Finly.

Ask for Aditya (runtime):
- Quick read: what architecture (hosted vs dedicated) will give us best chance to meet p95 <250ms for streaming with 300 concurrent streams at the average token lengths?
- Any immediate config suggestions (KV caching, batching profile, model quantization) and rough infra estimate (GPUs / pool size).
- List of telemetry/credentials you’ll need to run a faithful PoC.

Ask for Michael (commercial / capacity):
- Rough pricing delta between Hosted vs Dedicated for a 2-week PoC and a production footprint that supports 300 concurrent streams.
- Any special procurement / contract considerations for a short PoC that could convert to Dedicated.

Notes: John flagged cost sensitivity but will trade some cost for reliability if we can hit the SLOs.

Thanks — I’ll keep the Finly thread warm.

-Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Carter <john.carter@finly.com>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@finly.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency

John / Sara — thanks for the quick turnaround and the CSV. Per our internal sync, here’s a proposed PoC plan + answers to your questions. Attaching a 1-pager PoC proposal and a capacity estimate spreadsheet.

Short answers to your questions
- Hosted vs Dedicated: for the target SLOs (p95 < 250ms streaming + 300 concurrent streams) we recommend starting PoC on Redwood Dedicated reserved pool sized for your peak concurrency. Hosted can work for the initial exploratory tests, but Dedicated gives predictable tail-latency and isolation that’s important for streaming UX.
- Telemetry needed: sample traffic (you provided), a test API key or scoped service account for load testing, a list of representative prompts and expected quality checks, and a few synthetic user accounts for end-to-end flows.

Proposed PoC (2 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep): exchange creds, finalize test scripts, baseline run on Finly infra to confirm reproducibility.
- Week 1: deploy Dedicated PoC pool (GPU estimate in spreadsheet), run ramp + soak tests (validate p95 streaming, first-byte, and concurrency).
- Week 2: iterate on batching/cache config, measure quality delta vs current model, produce final report and recommended production config.

Target SLOs for PoC
- Streaming first-byte p95 < 150ms
- End-to-end token delivery p95 < 250ms
- Support 300 concurrent streams with <10% latency regression during 15-minute peak bursts

Next steps
1) Please confirm: agree to Dedicated PoC size + go/no-go on test account access (target start: 2026-11-08).
2) I’ll schedule a 30m technical kickoff with Aditya and your engineering lead.

Attachments: PoC-proposal.pdf, capacity-estimates.xlsx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
